route_name: Newarke Houses, a Lost King & High Cross
description: Link Leicester's surviving domestic history with Richard III's modern memorial and cathedral resting place before finding the medieval centre underfoot.
short_description: Old houses, a rediscovered king, a cathedral and a cross hidden in the road.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
recommended_age: Recommended 10+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A central walking route from The Newarke to High Street, close to the bus stations.

before_you_go.terrain: Paved streets and pedestrian areas through The Newarke, the cathedral quarter and High Street.
before_you_go.hills: Mostly level, with gentle street gradients.
before_you_go.steps: No museum or cathedral entry is required and the exterior route avoids mandatory steps.
before_you_go.accessibility: Outdoor checkpoints are reachable on public routes, subject to kerbs, city-centre works and event closures.
before_you_go.toilets: Check current museum, shopping-centre and council facility listings before departure.
before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable urban walking shoes should be suitable.
before_you_go.dogs: Dogs can join the outdoor route on a lead; check the High Cross venue’s current policy.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally suitable across the pedestrianised centre, allowing for crowds.

stops.Route: Newarke Houses, a Lost King & High Cross
stops.Cryptic_Clue: Begin where two old houses preserve stories of Leicester at home and at war.
stops.Hint_1: Head to The Newarke, south of the cathedral quarter.
stops.Hint_2: Find the museum formed from timber-framed and brick historic houses.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Newarke Houses Museum combines Wygston's Chantry House, dating from around 1511, with the later Skeffington House. Together they preserve rare domestic buildings in the city centre.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From outside, identify two contrasting building materials or ages.

stops.Route: Newarke Houses, a Lost King & High Cross
stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find the king with sword lowered, standing close to the grave he gained more than five centuries late.
stops.Hint_1: Walk north-east towards the cathedral gardens.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the bronze king beside Saint Martin's.
stops.Unlock_Fact: James Butler's bronze statue of Richard III was unveiled in 1980, decades before the king's remains were found beneath a Leicester car park in 2012.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Observe the pose and note whether the sword appears raised for battle or lowered.

stops.Route: Newarke Houses, a Lost King & High Cross
stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find the parish church that became a cathedral and finally received a king in 2015.
stops.Hint_1: The next checkpoint is beside the statue.
stops.Hint_2: Look for Saint Martin's cathedral and its spire.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The medieval church of Saint Martin became Leicester Cathedral in 1927. Richard III's remains were reinterred here in March 2015.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the public precinct, find one rose, crown or other royal symbol.

stops.Route: Newarke Houses, a Lost King & High Cross
stops.Cryptic_Clue: Finish where granite setts mark a vanished medieval landmark at the heart of the market town.
stops.Hint_1: Walk north-west to the meeting of High Street and Highcross Street.
stops.Hint_2: Find the food-serving pub beside a cross pattern laid into the roadway.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! Granite setts outside mark the site of Leicester's medieval High Cross, once the last surviving pillar of the old Market House. Check today's hours before stopping for food or a drink.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Find the cross shape in the paving from a safe pedestrian position.
